title: State matrix consolidation and auto-layout reset for UI kit
creator: Sophie Chen
description:
Problem: The UI kit contains many components where state variants are implemented as ad-hoc frames, local overrides, or nested groups. Over time this has caused inconsistent hover/pressed/focus behavior, broken auto-layout constraints, and confusing layer names. Publishing frequently introduces regressions because some components still rely on manual spacing fixes or deprecated token aliases.

Goal: Consolidate the component "state matrix" into a single canonical structure per component, reset and normalize auto-layout constraints across primitives (buttons, table rows, chart legends), and introduce a compact naming taxonomy so designers and engineers can reliably consume the library. Ensure the publish pipeline includes a preflight validation checklist to catch layout and naming failures.

Scope: Buttons (primary/secondary/icon-only), form fields, table row atoms, small charts legends and annotations, and a subset of frequently used utility components (badges, pills). This ticket covers design audit, component edits in Figma, a migration script plan for tokens/names where possible, and publishing with QA steps. Engineering-side implementation (SDK or codegen changes) will be tracked separately once the library is stable.

Approach:
- Audit and catalog every component instance that diverges from the canonical structure (capture as a spreadsheet with page URLs and node IDs).
- For each component family, define a single state matrix pattern (base / hover / active / disabled / focused) that uses component variants only for semantic states and relies on nested components for shared internals.
- Reset auto-layout on root frames and standardize spacing tokens (8/12/16 scale) at the component level. Avoid manual pixel nudges; use spacers when necessary.
- Establish a short naming taxonomy: <family>/<role>--<size>--<state> (e.g., button/primary--md--hover). Avoid deeply nested slashes and ambiguous adjectives.
- Create a pre-publish checklist and a small set of Figma plugin checks (component naming, missing constraints, manual transforms) that must pass before the library is published.

Risks & trade-offs:
- Rewriting many components will cause downstream breakage for in-progress designs; mitigation: provide a migration mapping and a deprecation window of 2 weeks with clear upgrade notes.
- Some icon-only and legacy components lack tokens; refactor will require collaboration with tokens owners (see dependencies).
- Full automation for renaming across instances is limited; expect some manual fixes for constrained edge cases.

Deliverables:
- Audited spreadsheet of divergent instances (CSV link below).
- Updated Figma library with consolidated state matrices for covered component families.
- Migration notes and mapping document for product teams.
- Publish checklist and release notes.
Acceptance criteria: All primary button variants use the canonical state matrix and pass the pre-publish checks
Auto-layout constraints normalized for table row atoms and chart legend components
Naming taxonomy applied to at least 90% of updated components
Migration mapping published and shared with product/design teams
No regressions in QA for core pages listed in the spreadsheet
tasks: Run audit sweep and produce CSV of inconsistent instances
Draft canonical state matrix patterns and validate with engineering
Apply auto-layout reset and spacing tokens to sample components
Perform bulk rename pass where safe; document remaining manual cases
Run pre-publish plugin checks and iterate until green
Publish updated library to team beta and collect feedback
Finalize release notes and schedule production publish
